attempts.prompt: Edit reference 1, a camera-accurate pose sheet, into master-quality BLACK AND WHITE INK LINE DRAWINGS of these four historical Chinese narrative-game characters. It is a transparent LOCAL cast layer for compositing on an existing period river street sketch. Ref 1 sets actor order, near-back viewpoint, proportions in frame and each action. References 2,3,4,5 provide canonical identities/costumes respectively for leftmost Wu Yi, young adult Chen Pingan, small girl Pei Qian, and elderly Zhu Lian. Preserve full bodies from topknots through entire shoes, four isolated cells, horizontal 1800:960 layout, all feet on a common baseline. Transparent outside (also between limbs), opaque WHITE paper inside contours, fine confident hand-drawn Chinese ink, selective broken light contours, black hair with white strand reserve, very restrained fine directional crosshatching in cloth folds. No wash, no grayscale blocks, no color, no background/ground/text/labels. Make natural believable individual people with different mass, poses, garment and height. Ref1 anatomical relations outrank frontal reference portraits: all viewed FROM BEHIND looking away along the street. In left cell elegant adult Wu Yi in long period robes, ornate modest crown, topknot and cascade of long hair; torso has just turned toward the throw, her LEFT arm stays down; visible RIGHT elbow travels diagonally down-right from shoulder, elbow lower than shoulder, right wrist recoils up-right, loose fingers release back left into depth. Sleeve cuff falls back so a slim section of forearm and the empty releasing hand show. A SEPARATE tiny wood-carved covered seedboat floats shortly above-left of the fingertips and distinctly above-right of crown base, exactly the location and small size of the seedboat in reference 1. No other boat. Make release feel light and recently completed, not waving or pointing. Chen Pingan is stopping, weight on planted foot and body slightly forward, tied hair, his period square BAMBOO traveling bookcase with woven bamboo texture and a small single gourd; Pei Qian a small double-bunned travelling girl settling behind Wu looking where the boat goes; Zhu Lian a lean slightly stooped old man, greying tied hair, modest travel robe, watching from the rear with a little profile. Translate the actual poses of the gray models into relaxed natural human joint angles, period garments, correct hands and foot anatomy. Four completed ink cutouts, physically separated for compositing. 白描人物线稿，衣褶贴合落脚重心，脸随镜头只露应见的一侧。

arguments.prompt: Precise local replacement part for the leftmost adult woman's raised RIGHT arm in image 1, for the back view in the riverside scene image 2; match Wu Yi in image 3. Output only ONE isolated woman's right forearm and right hand plus the narrow rim of the wide, falling silk sleeve at the elbow. A single entirely connected cutout, transparent outside, opaque white skin/paper inside with delicate black period ink linework. A close study drawn big, no other body parts, no person, boat, labels or diagram. Composition: a slender but adult forearm rising diagonally up-LEFT out of the cuff at bottom-right. The back of her right hand is seen obliquely from behind her toward the street; fingers continue the line of the forearm upward and slightly LEFT into the picture, reaching away after a light underhand toss. Natural slender level wrist, very slight pronation, backs of the knuckles continuing forearm, thumb relaxed on the anatomically correct side, fingers loosened with unequal staggered tips. Show two distinguishable profiles of index and middle fingers, ring and little fingers softly following; believable foreshortening, all fingers and thumb anatomically connected. Avoid hook wrist, claw, fist, pointing, V sign, splayed waving hand. The old arm curls back on itself; correct that. The arc goes from low-right elbow/cuff, along the exposed forearm, through the wrist, then towards upper left with the small hand. Black-and-white hand-drawn contours, sparing ink folds/hatching only at the cuff, crisp expressive silhouette to read when reduced. Use all the available canvas height. Only a short edge of the pale period sleeve at the bottom, include the complete fingertips at the top. No upper arm, no face, no floating decoration.

arguments.prompt: Use the attached four-panel reference board. Paint one finished isolated full-body black-and-white ink cutout of Wu Yi, the woman in B and D, in the NEW action from the REAR CAMERA in A. C is the same gesture viewed from the side for anatomical understanding, never the output camera. This is the quiet follow-through one beat AFTER she has tossed a very light carved seedboat several paces down a street AWAY from us. Strongly prioritize the change of silhouette and the body impulse, not another static back with the forearm bent up. On the left foot slightly forward already taking her weight, the pelvis settles diagonally over it. Her upper body leans into the depth of the street from the hips, the right shoulder blade travels forwards relative to her hips and the right shoulder is seen foreshortened, while the left shoulder, long sleeve and hanging left hand trail slightly back for balance. Asymmetric shoulders, clear natural contrapposto. Her gaze goes after the departing object slightly left and into the street. RIGHT arm reaches out from the right of her upper back, upper arm slightly down towards the right edge, lower arm goes mainly AWAY from camera; elbow nearly extended in 3D as in C but foreshortened as in A. In the drawing the right elbow is only a little LOWER than the shoulder, the wrist is a little higher than the elbow, the softly open fingers follow the wrist still further into the distance, thumb towards the midline, fingertips to the left of the wrist. A slim sliver of the underside/edge of the relaxing hand with staggered digits. Avoid a raised waving vertical palm, pinching, sign, wrist curled back towards herself, an elbow tucked against the hip, or a pointing index. The empty hand has actually released the object. No boat, objects or trail in this layer. Gravity still pulls the silk below her raised elbow; a few trailing sleeve folds, and hair & waist ties lag a little behind the moving ribcage. The costume silhouette, VOLUME of long hair, small elegant crown/hair knot and pearl ornaments, broad long embroidered silk robe, floor-length hem and simple flat shoes match B and D; face very largely hidden from behind. Spare, sensitive black and white narrative pen lines on opaque white inside the body, black hair with reserved fine white highlights, crisp varying dark contours; no color, no gray-painted volume, no labels, captions or ground. One natural dynamic person, entire coiffure through both soles, upright portrait canvas, centered with adequate margin. True transparent exterior. Output only the new ink artwork, no model or board.

References 2,3,4,5 provide canonical identities/costumes respectively for leftmost Wu Yi, young adult Chen Pingan, small girl Pei Qian, and elderly Zhu Lian. Preserve full bodies from topknots through entire shoes, four isolated cells, horizontal 1800:960 layout, all feet on a common baseline. Transparent outside (also between limbs), opaque WHITE paper inside contours, fine confident hand-drawn Chinese ink, selective broken light contours, black hair with white strand reserve, very restrained fine directional crosshatching in cloth folds. No wash, no grayscale blocks, no color, no background/ground/text/labels. Make natural believable individual people with different mass, poses, garment and height. Ref1 anatomical relations outrank frontal reference portraits: all viewed FROM BEHIND looking away along the street. In left cell elegant adult Wu Yi in long period robes, ornate modest crown, topknot and cascade of long hair; torso has just turned toward the throw, her LEFT arm stays down; visible RIGHT elbow travels diagonally down-right from shoulder, elbow lower than shoulder, right wrist recoils up-right, loose fingers release back left into depth. Sleeve cuff falls back so a slim section of forearm and the empty releasing hand show. arguments.prompt: Precise local replacement part for the leftmost adult woman's raised RIGHT arm in image 1, for the back view in the riverside scene image 2; match Wu Yi in image 3. Output only ONE isolated woman's right forearm and right hand plus the narrow rim of the wide, falling silk sleeve at the elbow. A single entirely connected cutout, transparent outside, opaque white skin/paper inside with delicate black period ink linework. A close study drawn big, no other body parts, no person, boat, labels or diagram. Composition: a slender but adult forearm rising diagonally up-LEFT out of the cuff at bottom-right. The back of her right hand is seen obliquely from behind her toward the street; fingers continue the line of the forearm upward and slightly LEFT into the picture, reaching away after a light underhand toss. Natural slender level wrist, very slight pronation, backs of the knuckles continuing forearm, thumb relaxed on the anatomically correct side, fingers loosened with unequal staggered tips. Show two distinguishable profiles of index and middle fingers, ring and little fingers softly following; believable foreshortening, all fingers and thumb anatomically connected. Avoid hook wrist, claw, fist, pointing, V sign, splayed waving hand. The old arm curls back on itself; correct that. The arc goes from low-right elbow/cuff, along the exposed forearm, through the wrist, then towards upper left with the small hand. Right foot ahead on screen right, left foot back on screen left; preserve the long separated stride and staggered sole heights, planted foot and slight bend to the knees. Light warm-weather outer travelling jacket, wrapped inner collar, short outer sleeves over inner sleeves, separate leggings and cloth bindings, thin rope belt, flat straw sandals and irregular tunic sides from B. Close to the young man’s back sits the historic open-top rectangular woven BAMBOO bookcase of C: four slightly projecting corner posts, cross-bars tied with twine, woven walls. A straw hat and spare sandals hang snugly at the side; one small waist gourd with a short tie and engraved curling motifs, at his anatomical LEFT waist, obscured naturally from this right-side camera if necessary. args.prompt: Render a single clean production-quality monochrome ink character layer for a historical Chinese illustrated visual novel. Panel A is the approved precise camera projection; copy all its visible angles and relative landmarks (top of head, shoulders, elbows, hand, pelvis, separate soles with near/far vertical offset). Character faces screen RIGHT, canonical right side camera, whole body visible. Panel B is the actual identity and costume reference. Hand-drawn varied dark contours and fine selective inner lines, sparse hatching, ink black hair with white strand reserves, white cloth and skin interiors. Strict black/white/neutral grayscale, no color, no scene, no ground line, no lettering, no keylines around the art. Isolated fully opaque subject interiors on transparent exterior for compositing. Only the single specified human, no board or mannequin. Draw Wu Yi alone, one full-length adult woman. Match face, brow, elegant nose and chin, long dark hair pinned in a small gathered crown with ornaments, dangling earrings, broad embroidered silk outer sleeves, waist ties, long layered skirt and flat closed shoes from the master. This is the quiet follow-through of a light underhand toss into the space in front of her. Legs stride in profile with the LEFT weight-bearing foot further RIGHT on screen and slightly higher, RIGHT foot trailing to the left; slight forward lean with the chest bringing the right shoulder through. Her anatomical right arm extends out toward screen RIGHT, elbow only slightly below shoulder, wrist a little ABOVE elbow, loose fingertips continue forward with the palm slightly up and turned sideways. Sleeve falls below the elbow with a graceful hollow shape. Far left arm hangs back and down, opposite the release. Keep vertical drop AND horizontal stride of both shoes, cuff edge, shoulder turn and projected hand in exact correspondence to A. Keep her facing right, show her actual side profile, no back view. Also draw ONE tiny separate carved walnut boat with upturned ends and a small pierced canopy, in side silhouette above/right of her fingertips, at the position and proportions in A. No lines of magic or speed. Retain white negative space between hand and boat. Leave clear exterior margin around all items. A single figure, a single detached boat.

undefined Draw ONLY Chen Pingan, lean young Chinese man about 20–22, using precisely the right-facing nose, eyes, narrow jaw, modest tied black topknot and plain horizontal hairpin in B. Exact single side profile and pose of block man A: youth checks his stride and focuses calmly to his right. His anatomical RIGHT elbow is low against his near side, right hand up gently holding the carrying strap at upper chest; no fist aimed forward. Left arm hangs easily on the far side. Right foot ahead on screen right, left foot back on screen left; preserve the long separated stride and staggered sole heights, planted foot and slight bend to the knees. Light warm-weather outer travelling jacket, wrapped inner collar, short outer sleeves over inner sleeves, separate leggings and cloth bindings, thin rope belt, flat straw sandals and irregular tunic sides from B. Close to the young man’s back sits the historic open-top rectangular woven BAMBOO bookcase of C: four slightly projecting corner posts, cross-bars tied with twine, woven walls. A straw hat and spare sandals hang snugly at the side; one small waist gourd with a short tie and engraved curling motifs, at his anatomical LEFT waist, obscured naturally from this right-side camera if necessary. No second gourd or waist purse. Keep pack on his back visible as the modest rectangular projection left of torso like A. Subject alone, entire hairpin and both whole shoes in the frame, no boat, no other people or objects in the air.

Render a single clean production-quality monochrome ink character layer for a historical Chinese illustrated visual novel. Panel A is the approved precise camera projection; copy all its visible angles and relative landmarks (top of head, shoulders, elbows, hand, pelvis, separate soles with near/far vertical offset). Character faces screen RIGHT, canonical right side camera, whole body visible. Panel B is the actual identity and costume reference. Hand-drawn varied dark contours and fine selective inner lines, sparse hatching, ink black hair with white strand reserves, white cloth and skin interiors. Strict black/white/neutral grayscale, no color, no scene, no ground line, no lettering, no keylines around the art. Isolated fully opaque subject interiors on transparent exterior for compositing. Only the single specified human, no board or mannequin. Draw ONLY Pei Qian, the small child traveller in B, in a natural right-facing side profile. Imaginatively turn her canonical face to the right, keeping the short lower face, straight brow, alert slightly almond eye, small nose, cheek fullness and the two practical tied hair buns with a few loose strands. Look toward a tiny boat above and ahead of her. Her chest and head lean forward from the hips with curiosity; do not turn her face toward camera. Reproduce arms from the block figure A, anatomical right upper arm drops along the rib cage, the forearm and relaxed hand hang slightly forward and low past the waist. Far arm slightly back and down for balance. Both legs visible in a small paused stride, right foot in front toward screen RIGHT. Same knee and foot heights as A. Child proportions distinct from adults, resourceful without caricature or exaggerated baby features. Detailed travel tunic with rope-belt, gathered rough sleeves, layered slightly worn split hem, cropped trousers with skin gap above cloth-wrapped shins, simple cloth shoes; small gathered SOFT FABRIC drawstring pouch on her anatomical left waist, largely occluded as natural. No gourd, other people, props in the air, or boat. Full head to feet.

Correct one structural mistake in the first ink cutout. Wu Yi must use the ARM CLOSEST TO THE CAMERA to toss, with the other one trailing on the far side. Image 1 incorrectly lets the foreground arm fall downwards. Swap which shoulder carries each action WITHOUT mirroring the woman: keep the profile facing RIGHT, the boat ahead at the right, the same overall body/feet pose, costume, face and camera. Draw the nearer anatomical RIGHT shoulder cap immediately below the visible ear. Connect THIS near shoulder to a broad sleeve extending across and IN FRONT OF THE CHEST toward screen right, ending in a partially exposed right forearm and a relaxed recently opened right hand at shoulder height, slightly up above the elbow. Show the continuous contour clearly from her near shoulder cap through the extended upper arm to cuff and fingertips. This near extended sleeve hides most of the upper bodice/lapel. On the far side of the ribcage, her other, LEFT upper arm is hidden behind the back and hair: only a modest far sleeve and the low relaxed far hand emerge BEHIND the back outline to screen left. Absolutely no near-side low sleeve in front of the body. Accurate side profile (viewer on her right), with only a very small portion of chest front visible. In pose terms she leans a little to screen right; RIGHT upper arm goes down a little from the shoulder to the elbow before the right forearm rises a little to the open empty hand. Her left foot is further screen right and slightly higher; right foot trails left. Keep the separate tiny seedboat in profile with its canopy, ahead and slightly up/right of her fingers. Keep both full shoes visible. Reference 2 locks her actual age, composed face profile, layered crown, long hair, earrings, flat shoes, long draped skirt and elegant broad robe sleeves. Pure thin BLACK INK outlines on WHITE paper interiors, sparse fine directional hatching, black hair with reserved fine white strands. White robes with just a few drawn embroidery lines; remove broad grey washed fills. No color, no scenery, no text, no small inset, no ground shadow. One isolated full body woman and one separated tiny carved boat. TRANSPARENT outside their opaque silhouettes.

Form and fabric folds defined by clean drawn contours. BLACK INK AND WHITE PAPER ONLY; neutral gray from line hatching allowed, absolutely NO blue, skin tones, red, brown or tinted grays. args.prompt: Draw ONLY Pei Qian in BLACK INK LINE DRAWING, a full length historical Chinese girl with two practical hair buns, isolated on transparent. A is the exact approved new walking pose, in a strict right-facing side view. B is her canonical face and everyday costume, C shows her prior profile and line style, not its old lean. Keep the lively almond-shaped visible eye, round young cheek, short chin, practical double buns, rope belt, bunched tied sleeves, ragged layered split tunic, small soft cloth pouch on the FAR left waist, cropped pants exposing a narrow strip of leg above wraps and simple black cloth shoes. Candid mid-step: the near RIGHT leg is directly under the pelvis with the whole right shoe resting flat and pointing right; the far LEFT knee bends, left shin trails diagonally BACK toward screen left, left shoe lifts entirely clear of the ground behind her, heel distinctly higher than its down-tilted toe. Keep a sliver of transparent space between the raised shoe tip and standing shin. Gently upright torso (roughly 6 degrees forward), chin raised very slightly and eyes watching an object a few paces ahead and slightly above. The near RIGHT shoulder leads a relaxed right arm down and forward of the hip, the distant LEFT arm is behind her, relaxed at her back, as in A. Keep the hands low and open, child taking half a step, no running, no exaggerated lunge. Do not plant both feet, do not spread the legs in a long stride. Whole head, fingertips and both shoes fully inside canvas. NO other people, boat, ground, shadows, motion lines, text, model or reference pictures. Pure dark fine pen outlines with expressive weight, very selective internal hatching, opaque WHITE interiors (especially clothing) and black hair with fine white strand highlights. White paper garments; omit dark gray filled panels, no color, no watercolor, no broad shadows. This is a character cutout for compositing.

args.prompt: Draw ONLY Pei Qian in BLACK INK LINE DRAWING, a full length historical Chinese girl with two practical hair buns, isolated on transparent. A is the exact approved new walking pose, in a strict right-facing side view. B is her canonical face and everyday costume, C shows her prior profile and line style, not its old lean. Keep the lively almond-shaped visible eye, round young cheek, short chin, practical double buns, rope belt, bunched tied sleeves, ragged layered split tunic, small soft cloth pouch on the FAR left waist, cropped pants exposing a narrow strip of leg above wraps and simple black cloth shoes. Candid mid-step: the near RIGHT leg is directly under the pelvis with the whole right shoe resting flat and pointing right; the far LEFT knee bends, left shin trails diagonally BACK toward screen left, left shoe lifts entirely clear of the ground behind her, heel distinctly higher than its down-tilted toe. Keep a sliver of transparent space between the raised shoe tip and standing shin. Gently upright torso (roughly 6 degrees forward), chin raised very slightly and eyes watching an object a few paces ahead and slightly above. The near RIGHT shoulder leads a relaxed right arm down and forward of the hip, the distant LEFT arm is behind her, relaxed at her back, as in A. Keep the hands low and open, child taking half a step, no running, no exaggerated lunge. Do not plant both feet, do not spread the legs in a long stride. Whole head, fingertips and both shoes fully inside canvas. NO other people, boat, ground, shadows, motion lines, text, model or reference pictures. Pure dark fine pen outlines with expressive weight, very selective internal hatching, opaque WHITE interiors (especially clothing) and black hair with fine white strand highlights. White paper garments; omit dark gray filled panels, no color, no watercolor, no broad shadows. This is a character cutout for compositing.

def chunks(b):

def chunk(t,b):return struct.pack('>I',len(b))+t+b+struct.pack('>I',zlib.crc32(t+b)&0xffffffff)
def itxt(k,v):return chunk(b'iTXt',k.encode()+b'\0\0\0\0\0'+v.encode())
